title: Your turn: pick the folder for Claude
learner: Same teacher, new task. This time you choose what Claude gets to see.

steps.text: Monday's task: a review quiz for Unit 4.

steps.prompt: Drag the folder Claude should work in onto the Claude window. You can also click it.

hints.Documents: That's your whole Documents folder: 1,240 files, most of them unrelated to this quiz. Can you give me something narrower?
hints.Biology: Closer, but Biology holds every unit plus your grading. Which folder has just what this quiz needs?
hints.Unit 3 – Cells: That's the unit we just finished. The quiz is for Unit 4.
hints.Unit 5 – Evolution: That's next unit's material. The quiz is for Unit 4.
hints.Grading: Grading has student work, not your Unit 4 notes. I'd leave it out unless you want the quiz based on past mistakes.

steps.fallback: That folder doesn't look like it holds your Unit 4 material. Try another one.

steps.text: Got it: Unit 4 – Genetics, 5 files. Your notes, the Punnett square worksheet and the reading are all here, and nothing unrelated. What should the quiz look like?
That's the habit: the smallest folder that holds everything the task needs.

steps.title: Nicely scoped
steps.text: Now do it with your own work. Pick the folder, then describe the outcome.
steps.prompt: Using the files in this folder, make a 10-question review quiz for Unit 4. Mix multiple choice and short answer, and add an answer key.
